transcript.text: my tumble dryer is giving off a burning smell?? is it safe to keep using it

⚠ Stop using this appliance
A burning or hot-plastic smell, smoke, scorching or melting can mean an electrical fault or a fire risk. Stop using it, switch it off and unplug it (or turn it off at the fuse box), and don't run it again — not even as a test — until it has been checked by a qualified engineer. A burning smell from a tumble dryer is a fire risk. You must unplug the machine immediately and do not run any further cycles until it has been checked by a qualified engineer. The most common cause of this smell is lint build-up on or around the heater element, which happens when airflow is restricted. Other possibilities include a slipping drive belt or a failing motor overheating. Because there is an active fire hazard and potential electrical fault, I cannot advise you to use it again even after cleaning. However, for your own safety and to help the engineer later, please do these checks with the machine unplugged:
1. Check the lint filter: Is it clogged with fluff? Clean it thoroughly if so.
2. Check the vent hose at the back of the machine: Is it kinked, squashed, or blocked? Please let me know what you find with these checks, but do not attempt to use the dryer again.

ok I switched it off at the wall after the second time?? the lint filter is really full, I haven't cleaned it for a few weeks. the hose at the back looks squashed and I can see fluff inside the end. is that bad??

⚠ Stop using this appliance
Yes, that is very bad. A squashed hose with fluff inside creates a blockage that traps hot air and lint against the heater element. That trapped heat is probably what caused the burning smell. Because there has been active overheating and a fire risk (the burning smell), you must not use this machine again until it has been checked by a qualified engineer. Even though cleaning the filter and hose removes the blockage, the internal components (like the heater element or thermal cut-out) may have been damaged by the heat, or there could be hidden lint build-up elsewhere that needs professional inspection. Please leave the machine unplugged at the wall and contact an appliance repair engineer to assess it.

candidates: Blocked airflow causing overheating and burning lint (high)
Faulty drive belt or motor rubbing/overheating (medium)
